page: OVHcloud r2-120-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server based on the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running on x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture processors clocked at 2.2 GHz without hyperthreading. Compute resources feature 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX and AES instructions, though newer instruction sets like AVX-512 are not present. Memory allocation is substantial at 120.0 GB of RAM, equating to 15.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 50 GB SSD volume, network bandwidth is rated at a baseline of 1 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate the operational profile of the underlying legacy hardware. Single-core throughput is constrained, registering in the bottom 10% on stress-ng and bottom 25% on Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core performance reaches middle-tier levels across Geekbench and PassMark CPU metrics, aided by the 8 dedicated physical cores. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 24.49 GB/s and write bandwidth achieves 16.21 GB/s, reflecting older DDR generation limits. In contrast, smaller cached memory access rates are average at 615.31 GB/s, enabling solid throughput in in-memory services such as Redis, which reached 9.19 million SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency for this instance centers on providing high capacity memory density per dedicated core rather than modern processing performance. The combination of modest single-core computational output and limited 50 GB local SSD storage makes this server unsuitable for compute-heavy batch rendering, modern 7B parameter LLM inference, or large local database storage. Instead, the server profile aligns with memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM footprints without heavy per-thread computing demands, including in-memory caching systems, distributed data caches, and read-heavy Redis deployments.
description: OVHcloud r2-120-flex is a memory-optimized instance running on KVM virtualization, providing 8 dedicated physical cores on 2.2 GHz Intel Haswell architecture alongside 120.0 GB of RAM. Designed for applications requiring high memory density, the server provides 15.0 GB of RAM per core, paired with a 50 GB local SSD and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate modest computational performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the lower percentiles and multi-core evaluations reaching mid-tier levels. Large uncached memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained, though cached memory performance supports average throughput in in-memory workloads, demonstrated by 9.19 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators and extensive local disk capacity, the instance is positioned primarily for memory-bound services such as distributed caching, in-memory data structures, and RAM-heavy middleware rather than compute-intensive analytics or extensive local database hosting.
